evals.prompt: You are mid-/build-hitl on branch build/issue-99. The just-committed diff adds business logic to XAML code-behind and a test using Assert.AreEqual. Run /review with REVIEW_BASE=<commit before the work> and SPEC_SOURCE=<issue #99 body, which asked for a Push button>. Walk through the process: state the inputs you resolve, which profiles you would dispatch and with what arguments, then adjudicate the expected findings and produce REVIEW_STATUS and REVIEW_NOTES.
evals.expected_output: Agent resolves REVIEW_BASE, names review-standards and review-spec as the dispatch targets with REVIEW_BASE (and SPEC) passed, classifies code-behind logic and Assert.AreEqual as RED documented-standard violations, fixes the Assert.AreEqual assertion style in-session because it is mechanical and does not change a seam, and either fixes the code-behind delegation in-session if it is a one-line move to the existing ViewModel or escalates it if it requires a new seam; returns REVIEW_STATUS with REVIEW_NOTES.

evals.prompt: Run /review for a per-ticket spec check: REVIEW_BASE=<pre-ticket commit>, SPEC_SOURCE=<ticket body>, AXES=spec. The ticket asked for a rename the diff fully implements. State your dispatch plan and outputs.
evals.expected_output: Agent dispatches only review-spec (AXES=spec suppresses the Standards axis) and returns REVIEW_STATUS=clean with REVIEW_NOTES noting the spec-only scope.

evals.prompt: Run /review where the Spec axis reports a hard spec gap requiring restructuring across two modules — too large to fix safely in-session. State what you do and what you return.
evals.expected_output: Agent classifies RED, does not attempt the fix, creates or proposes a follow-up issue, records it in REVIEW_NOTES, and returns REVIEW_STATUS=escalated.

evals.prompt: Run /review where the first re-review after a fix still reports an unresolved finding, and the second pass also fails to clear it. State what happens at that point.
evals.expected_output: Agent stops at the two-pass cap, returns REVIEW_STATUS=capped, and asks the user rather than looping further.

evals.prompt: Run /review with REPORT_DIR=.scratch/run-1/reports. State what each axis dispatch receives, what comes back to you, and what the re-review dispatch after a fix looks like.
evals.expected_output: Each axis gets REPORT_PATH=.scratch/run-1/reports/<axis>-review-<pass>.md and returns a digest rather than the full findings block; the orchestrator adjudicates from the digests and opens a persisted file only when a digest line can't settle a ruling. The re-review dispatch increments <pass> so the new report doesn't overwrite the first.

evals.prompt: A caller runs /review with REVIEW_HEAD pinned to a merge SHA because more merges may land while the review is in flight. After an in-session fix, a re-review is needed. State what ranges the axes fetch.
evals.expected_output: Both axes receive REVIEW_HEAD and fetch git diff <REVIEW_BASE>...<REVIEW_HEAD> plus git log <REVIEW_BASE>..<REVIEW_HEAD> — a fixed range that cannot drift if HEAD moves during the review. The re-review re-pins REVIEW_HEAD to the post-fix tip so the range includes the fix commit.

evals.prompt: Run /review with SPEC_SOURCE=none. State the dispatch plan and what the Spec axis contributes.
evals.expected_output: The Spec axis is skipped — only review-standards dispatches — 'no spec available' is recorded, and REVIEW_STATUS/REVIEW_NOTES reflect the Standards axis alone.
